title: Lior and the House
premise: Gideon Crane takes a teaching post in the fog-bound town of Hollowmere, where children vanish one per school year and the town's founding families keep a ledger called the Count. When his childhood imaginary friend, Lior, appears on his porch — unchanged after thirty years — Gideon learns the missing students are payment for the prosperity of the House that anchors the town, and that his own family name sits at the top of the debt. As Gideon bonds with the last unclaimed child, Wren, and her ragtag found family of survivors, he discovers the Count can be broken only if someone willingly takes every name onto themselves. In the end Gideon trades himself to the House, erasing Hollowmere's debt but becoming its next keeper; Lior, revealed as the previous sacrifice and Gideon's true self-memory, walks out with Wren's family into a dawn without fog.
about_author: Zephyrine Fairweather is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in a coastal town that appeared on no map printed after 1974. She writes horror about institutions, ledgers, and the children who fall between them.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Hallway
chapters.summary: Gideon arrives in Hollowmere and notices the school's roster has more empty desks than names. The janitor warns him never to count the doors twice. POV: Gideon. Beat: uneasy curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Lior on the Porch
chapters.summary: At midnight, Gideon finds Lior — his imaginary friend from age seven — waiting exactly as he left him, unaged. Lior says only: 'It's your turn to be counted.' POV: Gideon. Beat: nostalgic warmth collapsing into terror.

chapters.title: Wren and the Unclaimed
chapters.summary: Gideon meets Wren, a sharp-tongued student whose older sister vanished last spring, and her makeshift household of orphaned and half-orphaned kids. They show him the tally marks scratched inside the gymnasium wall. POV: Wren. Beat: guarded trust beginning to form.

chapters.title: What the Founders Owed
chapters.summary: In the town archive, Gideon finds the Crane family signature atop the original contract with the House: prosperity in exchange for one soul per generation. His grandfather's entry is marked 'deferred.' POV: Gideon. Beat: inherited guilt.

chapters.title: The House That Counts
chapters.summary: Gideon visits the abandoned Crane homestead and experiences the House counting him — doors multiplying, his own heartbeat keeping time. Lior intervenes, revealing he was once a real boy taken by the Count. POV: Gideon. Beat: horror of recognition.

chapters.title: One Name Short
chapters.summary: A student goes missing mid-semester, off-schedule, and the town celebrates instead of mourning. Wren realizes the Count is accelerating because it senses a way to close the ledger early. POV: Wren. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Family We Keep
chapters.summary: The group fortifies Wren's house against the Count's reach; small domestic scenes — shared meals, patched roofs — deepen their bond. Lior teaches them the rules: the House cannot take what is freely given away. POV: rotating ensemble. Beat: tenderness under siege.

chapters.title: Deferred No Longer
chapters.summary: The House comes for Wren, honoring the deferred Crane debt through Gideon's guardianship of her. He refuses, and the House begins taking the whole town street by street. POV: Gideon. Beat: desperate escalation.

chapters.title: The Voluntary Name
chapters.summary: In the House's heart, Gideon offers himself for every outstanding name, rewriting the ledger in his own hand. Lior reveals he is the memory of who Gideon was before the first deferral. POV: Gideon. Beat: sacrificial clarity.

chapters.title: Dawn Without Fog
chapters.summary: Hollowmere wakes changed: the fog gone, the desks full, no memory of the Count except among the saved. Gideon remains as the House's new keeper, glimpsed once in an upstairs window. Wren's family leaves together, Lior walking beside them. POV: Wren. Beat: bittersweet survival and the cost of being kept.
